prompt: You are a senior financial analyst at a major asset management firm. The portfolio manager for your consumer staples sleeve has asked for a quarterly performance review of Coca-Cola (KO). Using the attached XBRL financial data, prepare a quarterly variance analysis memo that compares the company's Q1 2026 performance against Q4 2025 (derived from full-year and prior-quarter data) and the full-year 2025 run-rate. Your memo should explain the key drivers behind the changes in revenue, gross profit, operating income, and net income, and comment on the trend in profitability margins. The deliverable should be a single Word document structured as a professional memo, with a clear header, an executive summary, a detailed variance analysis section with supporting tables, and a conclusion with implications for the portfolio.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
required_content: Summarize the key financial performance of Q1 2026
State the primary variance drivers vs. Q4 2025 and FY 2025
paragraphs: Coca-Cola reported Q1 2026 revenue of $12.47 billion, representing a solid start to the fiscal year. Compared to an estimated Q4 2025 revenue of $11.28 billion, this marks a quarter-over-quarter increase of approximately 10.6%. The company's full-year 2025 revenue was $47.94 billion, translating to a quarterly run-rate of approximately $11.99 billion, which Q1 2026 exceeded by about 4.0%. Gross profit and operating income also showed sequential improvement, though net income experienced a modest decline quarter-over-quarter, primarily due to higher selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses relative to cost of goods sold. Profitability margins remained robust, with a gross margin of 62.9% and an operating margin of 34.9% in Q1 2026, indicating stable operational efficiency.

sections.heading: Variance Analysis: Key Financial Metrics
required_content: Present a table comparing Q1 2026 to Q4 2025 and the FY 2025 quarterly average
Calculate and explain variances in revenue, COGS, gross profit, operating expenses, operating income, and net income
Derive Q4 2025 figures by subtracting first three quarters from full year where applicable
paragraphs: The following table details the quarter-over-quarter (Q1 2026 vs. Q4 2025) and year-over-year-run-rate (Q1 2026 vs. FY 2025/4) variances for Coca-Cola's core income statement metrics. Q4 2025 figures are derived by subtracting the year-to-date through Q3 2025 (data provided for Q3 2025 cumulative) from the FY 2025 totals. All figures are in millions of U.S. dollars.
**Variance Analysis Table (in millions USD)**
| Metric               | Q1 2026   | Q4 2025 (Est.) | QoQ Variance | QoQ % | FY 2025 Quarterly Avg | vs. Run-Rate | vs. Run-Rate % |
**Key Variance Explanations:**

**Revenue:** Q1 2026 revenue of $12.47 billion increased by $1.20 billion (10.6%) from the estimated Q4 2025 figure of $11.28 billion. The Q4 2025 estimate was calculated as FY 2025 revenue ($47.94B) minus Q3 2025 YTD revenue ($36.12B). Q1 2026 also surpassed the FY 2025 quarterly average of $11.99 billion by $487 million (4.1%), suggesting positive momentum into the new year.

**Cost of Goods Sold (COGS):** COGS in Q1 2026 was $4.62 billion, slightly lower than the estimated Q4 2025 figure of $4.72 billion (FY25 $18.40B minus Q3 YTD $13.67B). This modest decrease occurred despite higher revenue, indicating favorable cost management or mix. COGS was roughly in line with the FY 2025 quarterly average of $4.60 billion.

**Gross Profit:** Driven by the combination of higher revenue and stable-to-lower COGS, gross profit expanded significantly. Q1 2026 gross profit of $7.85 billion was $1.30 billion (19.8%) higher than the Q4 2025 estimate and $466 million (6.3%) above the annual run-rate, improving the gross margin to 62.9% from an estimated Q4 2025 level of 58.1%.

**SG&A Expense:** SG&A expenses declined meaningfully quarter-over-quarter to $3.47 billion from an estimated $4.20 billion in Q4 2025. This 17.3% reduction was a major contributor to operating income improvement and may reflect lower marketing spend or other discretionary cost controls. However, Q1 2026 SG&A was $158 million (4.4%) above the FY 2025 quarterly average of $3.63 billion.

**Operating Income:** The combined effect of robust revenue growth, controlled COGS, and sharply lower SG&A expenses resulted in a substantial increase in operating income. Q1 2026 operating income of $4.36 billion was $2.52 billion (136.8%) higher than the estimated Q4 2025 operating income of $1.84 billion. It also exceeded the FY 2025 run-rate by $918 million (26.7%), lifting the operating margin to 34.9%.

**Net Income:** Net income followed a similar, albeit less pronounced, trajectory. Q1 2026 net income of $3.92 billion grew by $1.65 billion (72.8%) over the Q4 2025 estimate of $2.27 billion (FY25 $13.11B minus Q3 YTD $10.84B). Compared to the FY 2025 quarterly average of $3.28 billion, it increased by $647 million (19.7%). The net margin was 31.5% in Q1 2026.

sections.heading: Profitability Margin Trend Analysis
required_content: Calculate gross margin, operating margin, and net margin for Q1 2026, Q4 2025, and FY 2025
Discuss the sequential and annual trend in margins
Link margin changes to the expense drivers identified above
paragraphs: Analyzing margin trends provides deeper insight into the quality of earnings. The table below presents key profitability margins for the periods in question.
**Profitability Margins**
| Operating Margin| 34.9%   | 16.3%          | 28.7%   |

The sequential improvement in all margins is striking, particularly the operating margin which nearly doubled. This is directly attributable to the favorable operating leverage: revenue grew while SG&A expenses contracted sharply on a quarterly basis. The gross margin improvement, while more modest, indicates stable or improving input costs and pricing power. Compared to the full-year 2025 averages, Q1 2026 margins are significantly higher across the board, suggesting a strong start to the year from a profitability perspective. The increase in SG&A relative to the annual run-rate is noted but did not materially impair the strong operating leverage demonstrated in the quarter.

sections.heading: Conclusion and Portfolio Implications
required_content: Summarize the key findings from the variance and margin analysis
State the implication for the portfolio manager's view on KO
Mention any notable balance sheet items as context
paragraphs: Coca-Cola's Q1 2026 results demonstrate a significant positive variance versus both the prior quarter and the annual run-rate. The primary drivers were robust top-line growth exceeding the FY 2025 pace, coupled with disciplined cost control that led to substantial operating leverage and margin expansion. The decline in SG&A expenses quarter-over-quarter was a major factor in the profitability surge.

From a portfolio perspective, these results are encouraging. The company showed it can grow revenue while managing costs, a key attribute for a mature consumer staples company. The strong start to 2026, with revenue and operating income well above their respective 2025 run-rates, supports a constructive view on the stock for the consumer staples sleeve. Balance sheet health remains sound; as of Q1 2026, total assets were $104.22 billion, stockholders equity stood at $33.63 billion, and cash and equivalents were $10.57 billion, all stable relative to year-end 2025. Diluted EPS of $1.00 for the quarter is consistent with the strong net income performance. The analyst will continue to monitor SG&A trends and revenue sustainability in the coming quarters.
